'''Robert John Hummel''' (born March 8, 1989 in [[Valparaiso, Indiana]]) is a former [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player at [[Purdue University]], located in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]].

==High school career==
===Valparaiso (IN)===
====2003–2007====
Robbie Hummel attended [[Valparaiso High School]] in [[Valparaiso, Indiana]]. Playing under coach Bob Punter, he played alongside his future college freshman teammate, Scott Martin (who transferred to University of Notre Dame after one season at Purdue). Hummel averaged 15.7 points, 7.1 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game as a Viking his Senior season.

==College career==
===Purdue===
====2007–2008====

Hummel attended Purdue University to play under head coach, [[Matt Painter]], and associate head coach, [[Cuonzo Martin]]. He averaged 11.4 points (2nd on team), 6.1 rebounds (1st) and 2.5 assists a game in his freshman year. Hummel led the [[baby boilers]], along with [[Chris Kramer]], [[JaJuan Johnson]], Keaton Grant, and [[E'Twaun Moore]] to a second place finish in conference play and onto a second-round [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearance, where they lost to a senior-led [[Xavier University|Xavier]] team. He broke the school freshman record with a 44.7 three-point field goal percentage, while leading the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He also recorded the highest free throw percentage for a freshman in school history with 86.5 accuracy, which led the team, and broke [[Kyle Macy]]'s 33 year old .859 mark. He was named ''First Team All-Big Ten'', becoming the first true [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Boilermaker]] freshman to earn the honor. He wrapped up his Freshmen season as 1 of 24 ''[[John R. Wooden Award]]'' finalists and of 10 finalists for the ''[[Oscar Robertson Trophy]]''. He helped lead the Boilers to a 25–9 overall season record.

====2008–2009====

Robbie Hummel completed his [[2008-09 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|sophomore season]] averaging close to 13 points (3rd on team) and 7 rebounds (1st) a game. As one of three tri-captains on the team and named the ''Preseason Big Ten Player of the Year'', he scored his 500th career point on December 13, '08 against [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]]. Robbie opened the season with ten straight double figure scoring performances, totaling 19 on the season (15–4), which included four 20+ point performances (3–1). He won back-to-back ''Big Ten Player of the Week'' honors in the month of December, pulling down a career high 14 rebounds and 25 points during that time frame. He recorded two preseason double-doubles, with one coming against [[Steve Curry|Stephen Curry]]'s [[Davidson College|Davidson]] team. Hummel began battling with [[back spasms]] and a broken [[vertebra]], which forced him to sit out 5 games and kept him from practice involvement. He had to wear a [[back brace]] in games following with limited minutes, while helping lead the Boilers to an 11–7 conference record, going 1–3 without him. Robbie led the Boilers to their first [[2009 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Big Ten Tournament]] championship in school history and was named the most valuable player of the tournament, following with a third straight [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearance and the program's first [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Sweet Sixteen]] appearance in 9 years. Finishing the season wearing a back brace, he scored a team high 17 points in the final game of the season against [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] in the Regional Semifinals. Although having dealt with performance-effecting injuries and missing four conference games, he was named a ''Third Team-All Big Ten'' selection.

====2009–2010====
[[File:20100123 Moore, Johnson and Hummel at a press conference.jpg|thumb|left|[[E'Twaun Moore]], [[JaJuan Johnson]] and Hummel at press conference (2010-01-23)]]
To start the [[2009-10 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|2009–10 season]], Robbie Hummel was picked as one of fifty players as a preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] candidate, along with teammate, E'Twaun Moore. He was a ''Preseason First Team All-Big Ten'' pick by both [[CBS Sports]] and [[Big Ten Network]] and a ''Preseason 2nd Team All-American'' pick by [[ESPN]] analysts, [[Doug Gottlieb]] and [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]]. Near mid-season, he was selected as one of thirty finalists for the [[Naismith Award]]. With MVP [[E'Twaun Moore]], Robbie was named to the 2009 [[Paradise Jam Tournament|Paradise Jam]] All-Tournament Team after a victory over #10 [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]]. During a school record-tying 14–0 season start on December 29, 2009 against [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], Robbie broke a school record, making 36 consecutive free throws, previously held by [[Jerry Sichting]]'s 34, which was set three decades earlier. He tied his former assistant coach, [[Cuonzo Martin]]'s single game school record of 8 three point-field goals made in a losing effort against an [[Evan Turner]]-led [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] team on January 12, 2010, in which he also scored a career high 35 points and received a dislocated [[pinky finger]]. In his team's tenth straight win in conference play at [[Minnesota Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] on February 24, Robbie injured his right knee in the first half after he slipped while attempting to plant his foot. He scored 11 points, making 3 of 4 three-pointers, in his prior twelve minutes of the game. Purdue officials reported the following day that Hummel tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) and would miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=4946559 |title=Robbie Hummel of Purdue Boilermakers out for season with torn ACL – ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=February 25, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref> He finished the last five games as a junior perfect from the free throw line, making all 21 of his attempts.
Playing in 30.3 minutes per game, he averaged 15.7 points (2nd on team), 6.9 rebounds (1st), 1.1 steals, 1 block, and 2.1 assists, while shooting 45.6 percent from the floor and led the Big Ten at 90.2 percent from the line, while also leading the nation amongst players at the forward position. He also shot 36.4 percent beyond the arc (2nd). Hummel scored at least 11 points in all but three games on the season (24–3), including ten straight, while recording eight double-doubles and being named a ''First Team All-Big Ten'' selection for the second time in his career at Purdue, while also being named a ''[[Fox College Sports|Fox Sports]] Third-Team All-American'', a ''[[State Farm Insurance|State Farm]]'' and ''[[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] Second Team All-American'', and an ''[[Associated Press]] Honorable Mention All-American''. He averaged 16.2 points and 7.3 rebounds per game in Big Ten Conference play for the #3 ranked team in the nation (12–3) and eventual conference titlists. Hummel received knee surgery and had to wait 4 to 6 months for the healing process.

====2010–2011====

After two consecutive seasons with performance-affecting injuries, Robbie was expected to return for his senior season. Fellow teammates JaJuan Johnson and E'Twaun Moore were returning as well, where they pulled out of the [[2010 NBA Draft]] to return for their senior season.  At team practice on October 16, Robbie tore the same ACL and was forced to sit out and serve as an assistant for the 2010–2011 season. Before the injury, Hummel was predicted as high as a ''Preseason Second Team All-American'' by much of the media.

====2011-2012====

Robbie Hummel returned to the team as a fifth year [[redshirted]] senior. On October 19, 2011, Robbie Hummel showed no effects from his injury during 3-on-3 fast break drills in practice. He was named one of 50 candidates for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], as well as the #24 player on [[CBSSports.com]] Top 100 List and a ''[[Lowe's Senior CLASS Award]]'' candidate to open the season. On November 11, the ''Preseason All-Big Ten'' selection scored 21 points, making 5 of 7 beyond the arc to open the season against [[Northern Illinois Huskies|Northern Illinois]] in 20 minutes of play. On December 3 in a three-point loss at #11 [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], Hummel suffered from [[cramp]]s and [[dehydration]], which eventually caused him to fall to the floor in the last minute of the game. Robbie led Purdue to a 10-3 non-conference mark and onto a 10-8 conference record. Hummel led the Boilers with 16.4 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per contest, while averaging 2 assists and .7 steals. He has scored in double figures in all but three games (1-2) this season, which included nine 20+ point games (7-2), while recording six double-doubles (4-2). On February 4, Hummel recorded a career high 5 blocks in a home loss to #20 [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]]. On February 22, he scored a season-high 29 points in a home win against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]]. Following that game and a 17 point performance win @ #11 [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], Hummel was named ''Big Ten Player of the Week''. In his last game at [[Mackey Arena]] on February 29, Hummel recorded a career high 6 assists, along with 26 points and 8 rebounds against [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]]. Throughout the month of February, Robbie led the nation in points scored. After the culmination of the regular season, Hummel was selected ''First Team All-Big Ten'' for the third time in his career, becoming the first Boilermaker since [[Rick Mount]] (1968–1970) to do so and the first Big Ten player since [[Mateen Cleaves]]. Hummel led the Boilers to a sixth straight NCAA Tournament, losing in his final game to Final Four-bound [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] in the Third Round by 3 points. Being guarded by [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]], Robbie scored 22 points in the first half, finishing with 26 points and 9 rebounds. He was named an ''[[Associated Press]] Honorable Mention All-American'' and also won the ''[[Lowe's Senior Class Award]]'' and the ''Thomas A. Brady Comeback Award''.

====Career notes====

Robbie Hummel became the 44th player in school history to score over 1,000 career points, surpassing the mark with a 13-point performance during a 73–66 loss{{cite web|url=http://content.usatoday.com/sportsdata/basketball/ncaab/game/Purdue_Wisconsin/2010/01/09 |title=Saturday, January 9, 2010 Purdue Boilermakers – Wisconsin Badgers Box Scores, Game Results & Summary |publisher=USA Today |accessdate=December 29, 2010}} at [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] on January 9, 2010.{{cite web|url=http://www.courierpress.com/blogs/college-sports/2010/jan/13/01132010/ |title=Purdue can't survive as a one-man team : College Sports : Evansville Blogs : Evansville Courier |publisher=Courierpress.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} On December 23, 2011 @ [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], Hummel became the tenth player in school history to tally 700 rebounds. His 90.2 free throw percentage on the [[2009-10 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|2009–2010]] season ranks second best in school history, just .5 percent under Henry Ebershoff's 44 year 90.7 mark. On March 4, 2012 with a 16 point performance in a loss @ Indiana, Hummel scored his 1,720th career point, placing him ninth in career points at Purdue. With a career marred by injuries and missing out on ten existing games during his sopohmore and junior seasons, Hummel missed out on likable chances to become a Consensus All-American, Big Ten Player of the Year, or to assist Purdue to a Final Four appearance. He finished his career with 1,772 points (9th), 862 rebounds (4th), 268 assists, 132 steals, 112 blocks, becoming the only Boiler to reach such numbers in each category.

===Team USA===
====2009====
With his lower back injury healing daily, Robbie was selected for the USA Men's [[2009 Summer Universiade|2009]] [[World University Games]] in [[Belgrade]], Serbia under [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] head coach [[Bo Ryan]]. Along with the likes of fellow Big Ten players [[Evan Turner]] and [[Talor Battle]], Hummel helped lead Team USA to the Bronze medal against [[Israel]], finishing with a 6–1 record. Pulling down a team single-game-high ten rebounds, he averaged 7.28 points and 3.4 rebounds a game.
